symbols.name: \mathcal I
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I=[\underline q,\overline q]\) with \(0<\underline q<\overline q<1\)

symbols.name: Y_i(a)
symbols.role: the nonrandom outcome of unit \(i\) under arm \(a\) in one infinite sequence of prefix populations

symbols.name: G_a
symbols.type: arm marginal of the limiting paired law

symbols.name: g_a
symbols.type: density of the limiting arm marginal

symbols.name: R_t^{\mathrm{aux}}
symbols.role: Any auxiliary draw used to construct an output at time \(t\) is generated by the known experiment randomizer, recorded in the observed history by time \(t\), and hence available to the procedure only through \(\mathcal F_t\); deterministic procedures set \(R_t^{\mathrm{aux}}=0\).

symbols.name: \mathcal F_t
symbols.role: The sigma-field generated by announced probabilities, assignments, observed outcomes, and every recorded auxiliary randomization through round \(t\). No unobserved potential outcome or unrevealed random seed is included.

symbols.name: L_t
symbols.role: An \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable function of the recorded observed history, including any \(R_i^{\mathrm{aux}}\) with \(i\le t\).

symbols.name: U_t
symbols.role: An \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable function of the recorded observed history, including any \(R_i^{\mathrm{aux}}\) with \(i\le t\).

symbols.name: \xi_{i,N}
symbols.type: randomization influence increment for the QTE

symbols.name: A_{a,N}
symbols.type: armwise average squared HT quantile loading

symbols.name: \widehat Q_{a,t}
symbols.type: generalized inverse of the shaped adaptive distribution estimator

symbols.name: \mathcal M
symbols.type: class of regular fixed prefix-population sequences

symbols.name: \mathfrak D_\varepsilon
symbols.type: class of known predictable two-arm randomization mechanisms

symbols.name: \mathbb P_{D,\mathcal Y}
symbols.role: The law of the assignment path and any recorded auxiliary draw generated by the known randomization mechanism \(D\) when the fixed sequence is \(\mathcal Y\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak B_\alpha
symbols.type: class of observed-data anytime-honest prefix-QTE bands

symbols.name: \mathfrak W
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak W(D,\mathcal C)=\sup_{\mathcal Y\in\mathcal M}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{\mathbb P_{D,\mathcal Y}}\mathfrak w(\mathcal C)\)

symbols.name: \mathcal Y^{\mathrm H}
symbols.type: explicit nonconstant-allocation Halton fixed potential-outcome sequence
symbols.def: Let \(u_i=\varphi_2(i)\) and \(v_i=\varphi_3(i)\). Then \(Y_i^{\mathrm H}(0)=M(u_i-1/2)\) and \(Y_i^{\mathrm H}(1)=-M/2+M[v_i+\{1-\cos(2\pi v_i)\}/(4\pi)]\).

symbols.name: d_{a,j}
symbols.type: limiting quantile derivative in the worked instance

symbols.name: p_0
symbols.type: minimax-width static allocation in the worked instance

symbols.name: s_0
symbols.type: dimensionless regret at the minimax-width allocation

novel.justification: This is a deterministic Glivenko--Cantelli condition on nested finite populations. It holds for low-discrepancy paired schedules, stratified population enumerations, and almost every fixed realization from a continuous paired law.

assumptions.condition: There exist \(L<\infty\), \(\beta\in(0,1]\), and an open neighborhood \(\mathcal U_a\supset Q_a(\mathcal I)\) such that \(|g_a(x)-g_a(x')|\le L|x-x'|^\beta\) for all \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and \(x,x'\in\mathcal U_a\).

standard.name: Local Hölder smoothness of the quantile density
Uniformly positive and finite density at target quantiles

novel.justification: The condition compares local increments of the step CDF rather than differentiating the step CDF at a jump. It holds for regular grids, low-discrepancy enumerations, and typical continuous-law realizations because individual jumps are negligible relative to the LIL scale.

This lattice-resolution condition only rules out prefix atoms of LIL-scale mass at monitored quantiles. It is satisfied by continuous-population enumerations with maximal multiplicity \(o(N\rho_N)\), including the explicit low-discrepancy witness.

definitions.name: Regular fixed prefix-population class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M=\{((Y_i(0),Y_i(1)))_{i\ge1}:\text{ Assumptions on bounded outcomes, paired empirical convergence, limiting density regularity, LIL-scale local spacing, and lattice negligibility hold for every prefix }N\}\)

definitions.name: Known predictable design class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak D_\varepsilon=\{(\pi_t,Z_t,R_t^{\mathrm{aux}})_{t\ge1}:\text{ the joint randomization mechanism is known, }\pi_t\text{ is predictable, }Z_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_t),\text{ and uniform overlap holds at every }t\}\)

definitions.name: Adaptive inverse-probability prefix-QTE process
definitions.construction: \(\widehat\tau_t(q)=\widehat Q_{1,t}(q)-\widehat Q_{0,t}(q)\), where each \(\widehat Q_{a,t}\) is the left inverse of the clipped monotone majorant of \(\widehat F_{a,t}\).

definitions.name: Explicit stitched CDF envelopes
definitions.construction: Set \(h_t=\log(16/\alpha)+2\log(1+\log t)\) and \(b_t=8(\sqrt{t h_t}+h_t)/(\varepsilon t)\); then set \(\underline F_{a,t}^{\mathrm{st}}(y)=[\sup_{x\le y}\{\widehat F_{a,t}(x)-b_t\}]_0^1\) and \(\overline F_{a,t}^{\mathrm{st}}(y)=[\inf_{x\ge y}\{\widehat F_{a,t}(x)+b_t\}]_0^1\).

definitions.name: Explicit stitched-inversion QTE band
definitions.construction: Invert the CDF envelopes by \(\underline Q_{a,t}^{\mathrm{st}}(q)=\inf\{y\in[-M,M]:\overline F_{a,t}^{\mathrm{st}}(y)\ge q\}\) and \(\overline Q_{a,t}^{\mathrm{st}}(q)=\inf\{y\in[-M,M]:\underline F_{a,t}^{\mathrm{st}}(y)\ge q\}\), using \(\inf\varnothing=M\), and set \(\mathcal C_t^{\mathrm{st}}(q)=[\underline Q_{1,t}^{\mathrm{st}}(q)-\overline Q_{0,t}^{\mathrm{st}}(q),\overline Q_{1,t}^{\mathrm{st}}(q)-\underline Q_{0,t}^{\mathrm{st}}(q)]\). Every displayed endpoint is a deterministic \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable function of \((\pi_i,Z_i,Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i\le t}\), and this construction uses no auxiliary randomization.

definitions.name: Observed-data anytime-honest prefix-QTE band class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak B_\alpha=\{(\mathcal C_t)_{t\ge1}:\mathcal C_t(q)=[L_t(q),U_t(q)],\ L_t(q)\le U_t(q),\ L_t(q),U_t(q)\text{ are }\mathcal F_t\text{-measurable for every }(t,q),\text{ every auxiliary draw used at time }t\text{ satisfies }\sigma(R_t^{\mathrm{aux}})\subseteq\mathcal F_t,\text{ and }\inf_{\mathcal Y\in\mathcal M}\inf_{D\in\mathfrak D_\varepsilon}\mathbb P_{D,\mathcal Y}(\forall t\ge1,\forall q\in\mathcal I,\tau_t(q)\in\mathcal C_t(q))\ge1-\alpha\}\)

definitions.name: Worst-case maximal LIL-normalized width
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak W(D,\mathcal C)=\sup_{\mathcal Y\in\mathcal M}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{\mathbb P_{D,\mathcal Y}}\mathfrak w(\mathcal C)\)

definitions.name: Allocation-regret and LIL-width frontier
definitions.construction: \(\Phi(r)=\inf\{\mathfrak W(D,\mathcal C):D\in\mathfrak D_\varepsilon,\ \mathcal C\in\mathfrak B_\alpha,\ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\sup_{\mathcal Y\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_{D,\mathcal Y}[\mathfrak R_N^\infty(\pi)]\le r\}\)

definitions.name: Observed-data primal--dual stitched-inversion handle
definitions.construction: Construct \(\mathcal A_\lambda\) by online mirror descent in the allocation coordinate against an adaptively discretized probability measure on \(q\in\mathcal I\). Form every gradient surrogate from \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable inverse-probability threshold scores and every band endpoint from \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable empirical-Bernstein CDF envelopes; if auxiliary randomization is used, record it as \(R_t^{\mathrm{aux}}\) before forming the output. Couple the allocation and inversion through realized intrinsic time.

definitions.name: Nonconstant-allocation Halton witness
definitions.construction: Let \(u_i=\varphi_2(i)\) and \(v_i=\varphi_3(i)\). Set \(Y_i^{\mathrm H}(0)=M(u_i-1/2)\) and \(Y_i^{\mathrm H}(1)=-M/2+M[v_i+\{1-\cos(2\pi v_i)\}/(4\pi)]\). The limiting latent pair is uniform on \([0,1]^2\); the arm-zero quantile derivative is \(M\), while the arm-one derivative is \(M+M\sin(2\pi q)/2\).

statements.statement: The explicit nonconstant-allocation Halton sequence \(\mathcal Y^{\mathrm H}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\). Its limiting arm quantile derivatives are \(Q_0'(q)=M\) and \(Q_1'(q)=M+M\sin(2\pi q)/2\), its rectangle discrepancy is \(O((\log N)^2/N)\), and its marginal jumps are \(1/N\); consequently the local-spacing and lattice errors are \(o(\rho_N)\).
statements.justification: One explicit regular sequence both certifies nonemptiness and creates genuinely different allocation optima across quantiles.
statements.gap: This is a construction-level feasibility certificate rather than a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: The exact two-quantile slice and the full frontier question use the same concrete nonconstant-allocation population.

statements.statement: For every arm \(a\) and threshold \(y\), \(M_{a,t}(y)\) is an \(\mathcal F_t\)-martingale with one-step conditional variance \((\pi_{i,a}^{-1}-1)\mathbf 1\{Y_i(a)\le y\}\). Moreover, for every \(N\) and \(q\in\mathcal I\), \(\xi_{i,N}(q,\pi_i,Z_i)\) is a martingale difference and \(\mathbb E_{D,\mathcal Y}[\xi_{i,N}(q,\pi_i,Z_i)^2\mid\mathcal F_{i-1}]=\ell_{i,N}(q,\pi_i)\).
statements.justification: This exact computation places allocation regret and QTE precision on the same randomization variance scale.
statements.gap: Dai, Gradu, and Harshaw analyze a scalar ATE loss; the threshold-indexed HT loading and mutually exclusive arm covariance are absent.
statements.consumer: The identity supplies the correct intrinsic time and the allocation-dependent gradient target for a frontier-seeking design.

statements.statement: The band \((\mathcal C_t^{\mathrm{st}})_{t\ge1}\) has deterministic \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable endpoints, uses no auxiliary randomization, and belongs to \(\mathfrak B_\alpha\). Its coverage is the binary-treatment, two-deterministic-policy, fixed-potential-outcome specialization of the importance-weighted counterfactual-CDF confidence bands in Mineiro and Howard, Section 3.4 and Theorem 3.4, and Waudby-Smith, Wu, Ramdas, Karampatziakis, and Mineiro, Section 4. The strict simplification is that it covers the exact realized prefix finite-population QTE \(\tau_t\), rather than a running averaged conditional reward distribution, and requires neither a reward-law model nor an off-policy regression nuisance.
statements.justification: The result records the exact design-based specialization needed by the frontier while making endpoint observability auditable.
statements.gap: Mineiro and Howard, Section 3.4 and Theorem 3.4, and Waudby-Smith, Wu, Ramdas, Karampatziakis, and Mineiro, Section 4, already supply time-uniform importance-weighted CDF inference; the contribution here is only the exact-prefix finite-population specialization and its nuisance-free two-arm inversion.
statements.consumer: Sequential trials can stop at any round while retaining simultaneous coverage of every monitored distributional effect.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(D\in\mathfrak D_\varepsilon\) and \(\mathcal Y\in\mathcal M\), \(\sup_{q\in\mathcal I}|\widehat\tau_N(q)-\tau_N(q)-N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\xi_{i,N}(q,\pi_i,Z_i)|=o_{\mathbb P_{D,\mathcal Y}}(\rho_N)\).
statements.justification: This reduction connects exact CDF inversion to the correctly normalized randomization influence process without differentiating a finite step CDF.
statements.gap: Zhang and Zheng establish fixed-horizon stochastic QTE-process linearization, not a prefix-population LIL-scale expansion under predictable assignment.
statements.consumer: The functional LIL converse can be proved on the linear martingale process and transferred to the QTE curve.

statements.statement: For every \(D\in\mathfrak D_\varepsilon\) and exactly every observed-data procedure \(\mathcal C\in\mathfrak B_\alpha\)—that is, each endpoint \(L_t(q),U_t(q)\) is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable and every auxiliary draw used by the procedure is recorded in \(\mathcal F_t\)—one has \(\mathfrak W(D,\mathcal C)^2\ge\sup_{\mathcal Y\in\mathcal M}\Gamma(D,\mathcal Y)\).
statements.justification: The converse now quantifies over precisely the implementable procedure class used by the frontier, including recorded randomization but excluding oracle endpoints.
statements.gap: Howard and Ramdas give an i.i.d. empirical-process LIL. Simchi-Levi and Wang characterize welfare regret versus power for scalar mean-arm gaps in stochastic bandits, not an LIL converse for an observed-data whole-QTE band under fixed potential outcomes.
statements.consumer: The result certifies the LIL-width coordinate of any proposed adaptive allocation and rules out uniformly narrower anytime bands.

statements.statement: Assume \(0<\varepsilon<1/3\) and \([1/4,3/4]\subseteq\mathcal I\). Evaluate the nonconstant Halton population \(\mathcal Y^{\mathrm H}\) at \(q_1=1/4\), \(q_2=3/4\), and static designs \(D_p\). Then \(d_{0,1}=d_{0,2}=M\), \(d_{1,1}=3M/2\), and \(d_{1,2}=M/2\), so the two quantile-specific oracle allocations are the nonconstant pair \(p_1^\star=3/5\) and \(p_2^\star=1/3\). Moreover, \(v_1(p)/M^2=9/(16p)+1/\{4(1-p)\}-5/8\), \(v_2(p)/M^2=3/(16p)+3/\{4(1-p)\}-3/8\), \(v_1^\star=15M^2/16\), and \(v_2^\star=21M^2/16\). Writing \(s=r/M^2\), the exact static variance frontier is \(\Phi_2(r)=\infty\) for \(s<s_{\min}\); for \(s_{\min}\le s\le s_0\), \(\Phi_2(r)^2/M^2=3/(16p_s)+3/\{4(1-p_s)\}-3/8\); and for \(s\ge s_0\), \(\Phi_2(r)^2/M^2=9/(16p_0)+1/\{4(1-p_0)\}-5/8\). Here \(s_{\min}=(2\sqrt3-3)/4\), \(p_s=\{15+8s-4\sqrt{s(4s+6)}\}/(25+16s)\), \(p_0=(9-\sqrt{57})/4\), and \(s_0=9/(16p_0)+1/\{4(1-p_0)\}-25/16\). Thus no static allocation can have zero two-quantile regret, and the exact minimum is \(M^2(2\sqrt3-3)/4\).
statements.justification: This exact slice replaces a definitional rearrangement with a strict positive-regret incompatibility theorem and a closed-form allocation attaining every point of the static variance frontier.
statements.gap: Li, Luo, Wang, and Feng optimize one selected quantile, while scalar Neyman-regret papers have one oracle allocation; neither computes a two-quantile frontier with distinct \(3/5\) and \(1/3\) optima.
statements.consumer: The solved slice supplies a calibration target and boundary conditions for any algorithm claiming to attain the full field-level frontier \(\Phi\).

statements.statement: Determine the field-level frontier \(\Phi(r)\) for every feasible \(r\), identify each exposed point by a dual probability measure on \(\mathcal I\), and construct a predictable observed-data procedure \(\mathcal A_\lambda\) whose allocation is \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable, whose endpoints are \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable, and whose auxiliary draws are recorded in \(\mathcal F_t\). Prove attainment and the matching converse uniformly over \(\mathcal M\).
statements.justification: The exact two-quantile calculation exposes the strict conflict, while the continuum frontier and an observable adaptive attaining rule remain the field-level open problem.
statements.gap: Li, Luo, Wang, and Feng optimize a selected quantile at a fixed horizon; Noarov, Fogliato, Bertran, and Roth optimize scalar ATE Neyman regret; Howard and Ramdas optimize i.i.d. quantile confidence-sequence width. None characterizes this joint frontier.
statements.consumer: Trial designers obtain a certified rule for each admissible trade-off between allocation efficiency and optional-stopping-valid distributional precision.

statements.statement: Suppose \(A_{1,N}(q)=A_{0,N}(q)>0\) for every \(N\) and \(q\in\mathcal I\). Then the unique minimizer of \(p\mapsto N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\ell_{i,N}(q,p)\) is \(p^\star_N(q)=1/2\). Under balanced assignment, \(V_N(q;1/2)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\{c_{i,1,N}(q)+c_{i,0,N}(q)\}^2\) and \(\mathfrak R_N^\infty(1/2)=0\); thus the variance coordinate collapses to the classical balanced two-arm martingale LIL normalization.
statements.justification: This explicit calculation checks the corrected loss, oracle, regret, and LIL normalization in a nonempty symmetric case.
statements.gap: This is the required sanity reduction rather than an independent novelty claim.
statements.consumer: Implementers can validate the general allocation loss against balanced randomization before deploying the frontier-seeking procedure.

sampling_model.design: A known randomization device announces predictable \(\pi_t\), generates \(Z_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_t)\), and records any auxiliary draw \(R_t^{\mathrm{aux}}\) in \(\mathcal F_t\) before a band is reported.
sampling_model.units: One infinite fixed potential-outcome sequence whose first \(t\) units form the finite population at monitoring time \(t\); the only randomness is treatment assignment.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment reveals only \(Y_t^{\mathrm{obs}}\); every reported endpoint is a measurable function of the observed filtration and no missing potential outcome enters a procedure.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The coverage specialization uses no outcome-regression nuisance. The full frontier handle estimates local quantile spacing only from observed inverse-probability threshold scores and confidence sequences.

estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_t(q)=\widehat Q_{1,t}(q)-\widehat Q_{0,t}(q),\qquad \Phi(r)=\inf_{D,\mathcal C:\,\limsup_N\sup_{\mathcal Y}\mathbb E_{D,\mathcal Y}\mathfrak R_N^\infty\le r}\mathfrak W(D,\mathcal C)\)

Relevant locator: abstract, Section 3.1, and Theorem 3.2.

Yichong Zhang and Xin Zheng (2020), Quantile Treatment Effects and Bootstrap Inference under Covariate-Adaptive Randomization, Quantitative Economics 11(3), 957--982. Relevant locator: abstract and introduction.

Vitor Hadad, David A. Hirshberg, Ruohan Zhan, Stefan Wager, and Susan Athey (2021), Confidence Intervals for Policy Evaluation in Adaptive Experiments, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 118(15), e2014602118. Relevant locator: abstract and significance statement.

David Simchi-Levi and Chonghuan Wang (2024), Multi-Armed Bandit Experimental Design: Online Decision-Making and Adaptive Inference, Management Science 71(6), 4828--4846; published online September 20, 2024, in the issue dated June 2025. Relevant locator: abstract and article information.
Aad W. van der Vaart (1998), Asymptotic Statistics, Cambridge University Press. Relevant locator: Chapter 21, Quantiles and Order Statistics, pp. 304--315, especially Section 21.2.

Ian Waudby-Smith, Lili Wu, Aaditya Ramdas, Nikos Karampatziakis, and Paul Mineiro (2024), Anytime-valid Off-policy Inference for Contextual Bandits, ACM/IMS Journal of Data Science 1, Article 3; first circulated in 2022 as arXiv:2210.10768. Relevant locator: Section 4, Time-Uniform Inference for the Off-Policy CDF.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Derives a quantile-specific design-based efficiency bound and response-adaptive allocations attaining it at a fixed horizon.
Theorem 3.2 gives anytime near-logarithmic Neyman regret for design-based scalar ATE estimation relative to the hindsight-optimal fixed allocation under strengthened outcome conditions.
Gives simultaneous time-and-quantile confidence sequences with the square-root log-log time rate for an i.i.d. quantile process.
Section 3.4, especially Theorem 3.4, gives time- and value-uniform importance-weighted CDF bands for running averaged conditional counterfactual distributions under nonstationarity.
Characterizes Pareto-optimal experiments for the trade-off between participant-welfare regret and statistical power for gaps between mean arm outcomes in a stochastic multi-armed bandit.
Establishes fixed-horizon weak convergence uniformly in quantile index and bootstrap QTE bands under covariate-adaptive randomization.
Section 4 constructs anytime-valid, variance-adaptive confidence bands for the entire off-policy reward CDF under adaptive logging.

tldr: One response-adaptive experiment must serve a continuum of quantiles whose variance-optimal allocations disagree. The focal object is \(\Phi(r)\), the smallest worst-case LIL-normalized width of an observable anytime-valid prefix-population QTE band at whole-curve Neyman regret at most \(r\). Every admissible endpoint and auxiliary draw is now explicitly recorded in \(\mathcal F_t\), the coverage result is only an exact-prefix finite-population specialization of existing counterfactual-CDF confidence bands, and the lower bound is stated over that same procedure class. A nonconstant Halton population yields a fully computed two-quantile frontier with oracle allocations \(3/5\) and \(1/3\) and a strictly positive minimum simultaneous regret; the continuum frontier remains the first-class open question.

project_justification.gap: Existing importance-weighted CDF confidence bands already provide broad anytime validity, and fixed-horizon quantile design optimizes one selected quantile. The missing theorem-level object is the allocation-regret versus LIL-width boundary when several quantile-specific oracle allocations conflict.
project_justification.niche: The niche is an observed-data design-based Pareto frontier whose regret and inference coordinates are linked by the same threshold-indexed predictable variance and whose finite-dimensional sections can be computed exactly.
project_justification.fill: The project specializes existing CDF confidence-band technology to exact prefix finite-population QTEs, proves the converse for precisely measurable procedures, computes a nonconstant two-quantile frontier, and isolates continuum attainment as the open field-level problem.

related_work: Mineiro and Howard, Section 3.4 and Theorem 3.4, give time- and value-uniform importance-weighted bands for running averaged conditional counterfactual CDFs under nonstationarity; the coverage theorem here is a fixed-potential-outcome, binary-treatment specialization with the strict simplification of exact realized-prefix targets and no reward-law or regression nuisance. Waudby-Smith, Wu, Ramdas, Karampatziakis, and Mineiro, Section 4, give variance-adaptive confidence bands for the entire off-policy reward CDF, uniform in time and quantile level; that result likewise supplies general confidence-sequence technology rather than a theorem-level target to beat. Li, Luo, Wang, and Feng, in the sections headed Design-based optimal variance lower bound and Theoretical property, motivate quantile-targeted response adaptation and fixed-horizon efficiency for one selected QTE; the two-quantile theorem isolates the allocation incompatibility absent from that single-target result. Dai, Gradu, and Harshaw, Section 4.1, Definition 1, and Noarov, Fogliato, Bertran, and Roth, Section 3.1 and Theorem 3.2, develop scalar ATE Neyman regret and inform the online loss analysis. Howard and Ramdas, equations (1)--(2) and Theorem 2, derive i.i.d. quantile confidence sequences and inform the LIL normalization. Zhang and Zheng establish fixed-horizon QTE-process asymptotics and bootstrap inference uniformly over a compact quantile-index set, informing the Bahadur comparison. Simchi-Levi and Wang, published online in 2024 and appearing in Management Science 71(6) in 2025, characterize a Pareto trade-off between participant-welfare regret and statistical power for scalar gaps between stochastic arm means. That article informs the frontier viewpoint, whereas \(\Phi\) concerns fixed potential outcomes, whole-curve QTE Neyman regret, and LIL-normalized anytime-band width. Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas, in the Third Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning, PMLR 236, Section 2.2, equations (3)--(4), provide the propensity-truncation reference for fixed overlap and develop adaptive A2IPW inference. Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey develop adaptively weighted augmented inverse-propensity inference for policy evaluation.
technical_internal_limitation: The regular core excludes atoms and vanishing-density cusps. The explicit coverage band is a conservative specialization of existing counterfactual-CDF confidence bands and is not claimed to attain \(\Phi\). The exact formula for \(\Phi_2\) concerns a static two-quantile slice on one explicit population; it is a worked boundary condition, not the continuum solution.
honest_scope: The observable coverage specialization, LIL-scale Bahadur reduction, procedure-matched functional lower bound, nonempty construction, and exact two-quantile frontier are statements to prove. The exact field-level \(\Phi\), its dual active-quantile measure, and an adaptive observable procedure attaining it uniformly over \(\mathcal M\) remain open. In the homogeneous-loading special case, balanced assignment still recovers the classical two-arm martingale LIL normalization.
novelty_justification: The novelty is not the existence of an anytime CDF band: Mineiro and Howard and Waudby-Smith, Wu, Ramdas, Karampatziakis, and Mineiro already provide that general technology. The theorem-level advance is the allocation-inference boundary created by incompatible quantile-specific randomization optima, beginning with an exact nonconstant two-quantile section and a converse over precisely observable procedures. The field-level object \(\Phi\) extends this conflict to a continuum and remains openly constructive.
